approachQuestion.prompt:
Highest balance reached during a sequence

A wallet starts at zero. The array changes lists deposits as positive integers and withdrawals as negative integers, in the exact order they occurred. Return the greatest balance reached after any event, including the starting balance before the first event. The event order is part of the input meaning. Do not modify the caller-owned array. Return one integer.

Constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; −1,000,000,000 ≤ changes[i] ≤ 1,000,000,000. The running sum fits in a signed 64-bit integer.

Examples:
1. changes = [8, -11, 6, 4] → 8 (balances: 0, 8, -3, 3, 7).
2. changes = [-4, -2, -1] → 0 (the starting balance remains the maximum).

Choose one method that returns the required value for every allowed input and preserves the caller’s array.
constraints: Prefix means the first k events in their original order, for 0 ≤ k ≤ n.
Sorting or otherwise reordering events changes the sequence being measured.
Do not mutate the caller-owned changes array.
For every prefix k, the absolute running sum is at most 200,000,000,000,000 and fits in a signed 64-bit integer.

options.text: Visit events in order, update one running balance, and retain the largest balance seen, starting from zero.
options.feedback: The balance after each prefix is exactly the running sum; a running maximum covers all prefixes without changing event order.

options.text: Build an array containing the balance after every event, then find the largest value together with the initial zero.
options.feedback: This is correct for every allowed sequence and respects its order, but the full list of prefix balances is unnecessary when only the maximum is returned; keep one running maximum instead.

options.text: Sort the changes from largest to smallest, then compute the maximum running balance.
options.feedback: The order defines the prefixes. For [8, -11, 6, 4], the true maximum is 8; sorting gives [8, 6, 4, -11] and a maximum of 18.

options.text: Add all events and return the final balance.
options.feedback: The final balance can be below an earlier peak. For [8, -11, 6, 4], the final balance is 7 but the maximum reached is 8.

feedback.reason: The method must satisfy the complete input/output contract, including required order and mutation behavior.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed below—scan events in their original order while keeping only the running balance and best balance—choose its worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Exclude the caller’s input and the one-number result. Arithmetic is constant-time for the stated 64-bit values.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) additional space

feedback.reason: Each event is processed once and updates only two scalar values, so the method uses constant auxiliary space. Storing every prefix balance uses linear space; recomputing each prefix from the start takes quadratic time; sorting is irrelevant and would violate the event-order contract.

methodReveal.title: Preserve event order with a running peak
methodReveal.description: Start the balance and best-so-far value at zero. Read each change in its given position, add it to the balance, and update the best-so-far value. Keeping only these two values preserves the exact prefix meaning without storing prior balances.
